name: CAISO
desc: Positions engaging the California ISO (CAISO) specifically.

letters.org: California Department of Water Resources State Water Project
letters.desc: DWR, the largest single load in CAISO markets, describes CAISO's ongoing real-time load bidding initiative as the right tool for unlocking curtailable load capacity, and notes it could offer approximately 2,600 MW of curtailable pumping load if the functionality is restored.
quotes: If CAISO implements real-time load bidding, DWR can provide approximately 2,600 MW of available curtailable load, because the State Water Project's water pumping operations are curtailable in response to market signals.
Unlocking the curtailability of existing loads requires no upgrades or increased ratepayer costs—it simply requires new market functionality.

letters.desc: Federal study and prioritization requirements would conflict with CAISO's recently approved interconnection process enhancements and the three-year study horizon in the ANOPR is insufficient for California system conditions.
quotes: adding this new layer of study processes would impact CAISO's recent interconnection process enhancements, approved by FERC last year, and their interaction with the CAISO Transmission Planning Process (TPP).
in California's experience, studies looking out only three years would likely be insufficient to fully assess system conditions, load growth, and potential reliability impacts.

letters.desc: Fluence opposes CAISO's rule that caps a BESS resource's regulation capacity at its inverter rating, arguing this leaves up to half of the resource's regulation capability unused and harms both resource economics and system efficiency.
quotes: By artificially restricting regulation capacity to equal the inverter rating, CAISO is leaving 50% of the BESS resource's regulation capability unutilized, harming both resource economics and system efficiency.

letters.desc: CAISO describes its existing collaborative planning framework with the CEC and CPUC, including a 2022 MOU for incorporating large load demand forecasts into transmission planning. CAISO notes this regional model supports the goals of the ANOPR and asks that any rule preserve the independent entity standard.
quotes: The longstanding approach of enabling transmission providers to propose tailored processes to meet regional needs under the independent entity standard will allow transmission providers to tailor their studies to ensure the orderly and timely interconnection of large loads.

letters.desc: ETI documents chronic and severe CRR underfunding in CAISO, with underfunding exceeding 100% on dozens of constraints and totaling hundreds of millions of dollars. The filing argues this undermines forward price signals that developers rely on to hedge infrastructure investments.
quotes: underfunding levels approaching and often exceeding 100%
[u]nderfunding uncertainty increases risk and lowers the expected CRR value in the auction, depressing CRR bid prices and reducing the value of ARRs.
Developers are using CRRs and the instruments need to function and price appropriately to for developers to properly hedge physical exposure.

letters.desc: TBA cites CAISO's position that only fully curtailable or dispatchable loads should qualify for expedited study as evidence supporting a strict eligibility threshold for non-firm service.
quotes: only loads that are "completely curtailable or dispatchable" should qualify for expedited interconnection study treatment, underscoring that the depth of flexibility determines whether a project can be evaluated without peak-driven upgrades

letters.desc: Verrus cites CAISO's comments as supporting the position that curtailable loads are easier to study and interconnect, and endorses CAISO's call for strict curtailment protections.
quotes: Verrus agrees with the California Independent System Operator ("CAISO") and Transmission Access Policy Study Group ("TAPS") that "strict, unwavering protections" are necessary to ensure that flexible loads meet their curtailment obligations.
